Introduction
The enemies are at the gates Brothers!
We are assailed on all sides. Go, tell them in the city, that these fiends will have no satisfaction while we stand. They that seek our destruction, shall rue setting their course against us, for we shall reap upon them a terrible price for their presumption.
Mithras Grant us Strength!
Malleus Deum is a player-facing, medium complexity, low-fantasy, pen and paper, tabletop role-playing game (TTRPG) set in a grimdark, late medieval analog setting.
{% include "docs/sidebars/player_facing_rules.xml" %}
Player
In the context of these rules we use the term Player to refer to those people playing the game who control a Player Character, specifically not including the GM. We do this because it is convenient to distinguish between the Players and GM since they perform very different roles in the game, but also for historical reasons. TTRPGs evolved from wargames some of which had referees whose role was primarily to make rules arbitrations, they were not players in the technical sense. The role of GMs in TTRPGs evolved from the role of referees in wargames.
Player Character (PC)
A fictional Character in the game whose actions are directly controlled by a Player. The PCs are the protagonists in the game.
Character
A Character is person or monster in the game, this includes all PCs and all NPCs. Characters have motivations. Hazards, aspects are not characters.
PC See Player Character
Player Facing
Player facing rules follow the idea that players should be the one driving the action in the game. A player facing combat system for instance has the player rolling to both hit and avoid being hit.
Protagonist
A synonym for PCS. Fictional characters in the game whose actions are directly controlled by a player. The PCs/Protagonists are opposed in the game by their Antagonists.
Anagonists
Antagonist
An antagonist is a person, group, or force that opposes, struggles against, or competes with the protagonists in a story, creating conflict and tension. In a TTRPG the NPCs, Monsters, the Environment and other hazards form the antagonists. The GM controls the antagonists in the game.
Game Master (GM)
The GM facilitates the game, by directing the story, controling the non-player characters (NPCs), describing the world, acting as a referee for the rules, and guiding players through an interactive narrative.
NPC See Non-Player Character
Hazards
Hazards are antagonists that are not characters, traps, obstacles, snow storms, raging rivers and so on.
TTRPGs like Malleus Deum are games that lie somewhere on a spectrum between collaborative story-telling on one side, and detailed combat simulation on the other. Malleus Deum aims to be equal parts story simulator and combat simulator. Neither overly narrative and abstract in nature, nor overly technically crunchy.
During the game, players control an individual character within the fictional world, called a Player Character or PC. Each player creates their own PC using a Character Sheet that describes the character's abilities, strengths and weaknesses. Instructions for creating PCs can be found in Chapter ch:character-creation on pagech:character-creation
One person assumes the role of Game Master or GM, acting as the referee or narrator in the game. During play the GM controls all the Anagonists while the players control the Protagonists, PCs. The Antagonists include all the other characters within the story, the monsters, the traps and obstacles in the world and pretty much anything the characters can come into conflict with or that has to be overcome by the PCs. More specifically, we call the characters and monsters that the GM controls Non-Player Characters or NPCs. While all other non-character antagonists are Hazards. We use the term Character to denote both player characters and non-player characters.
Most interesting narrative decisions within the game are made by players rolling dice to make Checks defined by their Abilities. The character sheets list the abilities available to each PC. The process by which checks are laid out in Chapter ch:checks on pagech:checks. There is a list of available abilities in Chapter ch:abilities on pagech:abilities.
Keywords and Conditions are game concepts designed to tie informal descriptive elements of the game to formal rules. For instance a room might be dark, a keyword, and a character might be blinded, a condition (all conditions are also keywords). Keywords and Conditions are described further in Chapterch:keywordsandconditions on pagech:keywordsandconditions.
Throughout the rest of this book we will illustrate game mechanics using blocks of example text such as this one. We will use two PCs in these examples: Dourli, intrepid dwarven warrior; and Rozlyn, shadowy cutpurse and sometime dabbler in the dark arts.
In order to avoid verbage, we will take Dourli to mean either the PC Dourli, or the Player who controls Dourli. It is up to the reader to distinguish which of the two meanings is intended from context.
The details of how this all fits together, how to create a character, how to make checks, and more is covered in the next few chapters.
